---
title: Single sign-on and SAML
description: Signing in to masks with another service, signing SAML applications in with masks, and provisioning actors over SCIM.
---

masks works with other sign-in services in three ways. Single sign-on (SSO) means an actor signs in
once and uses that sign-in for many apps.

| Direction | masks is | See |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in to masks with Google, Okta, Entra, or a SAML identity provider | the service provider, the side that accepts the sign-in | [Providers](#providers) |
| Sign in to a SAML-only app, such as a wiki, with masks | the identity provider, the side that signs actors in | [SAML applications](#saml-applications) |
| Keep masks' actors in sync with a directory | the SCIM service, the side a directory sends changes to | [Provisioning](#provisioning) |

## Providers

A provider is another service that actors sign in with, over OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, or
SAML 2.0. masks links the account there to an actor in masks. That link is a **connected account**.

A provider takes the place of the password. The actor's
[sign-in policy](/build/features/#sign-in-policies) still asks for a second factor when it requires
one.

To add a provider, open **Settings**, then **Providers**, in `/manage`, and choose **Add provider**.
[A provider's page](/build/manage/#a-providers-page) lists what each tab holds.

### Known providers

A known provider fills in every setting except the credentials.

| Known provider | Protocol | Asks for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google | OpenID Connect | |
| Microsoft | OpenID Connect | directory (tenant) ID |
| Apple | OpenID Connect | team ID, key ID, private key |
| GitHub | OAuth 2.0 | |
| GitLab | OpenID Connect | domain, `gitlab.com` by default |
| Slack | OpenID Connect | |
| LinkedIn | OpenID Connect | |
| Discord | OAuth 2.0 | |
| Facebook | OAuth 2.0 | |
| X | OAuth 2.0 | |
| Okta, Auth0 | OpenID Connect | domain |
| Keycloak | OpenID Connect | domain, realm |
| Microsoft Entra (SAML), Okta (SAML), Google Workspace (SAML) | SAML 2.0 | metadata |
| Notion (MCP) | MCP | Nothing. masks registers itself. |

Under **Anything else**, a blank OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, or MCP server provider asks for
everything.

Google, Apple, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, LinkedIn, and Discord turn on **Trust the addresses it
confirms**.

An MCP server signs nobody in. Apps use it through a
[delegation](/build/connecting-via-sdk/#delegation).

### Provider roles

**Add the actors it signs in**, on the provider's **Sign-in** tab, sets its role. The manage API
names the two roles `delegate` (on) and `credential` (off).

| | Off (`credential`) | On (`delegate`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Someone with no account | Refused. | Becomes an actor, with **Scopes a new actor holds**. |
| Name, photo, and email address | Left alone. | Updated from the provider on every sign-in. |

Turn it on when the company directory decides who works there.

Under either role:

- An actor who already has the same email address is connected only when both masks and the
  provider confirm that address, and only after the actor signs in another way once.
- An invited actor who has not accepted yet is connected at once, but only when masks
  [trusts the address](#trusted-email-addresses).

### Trusted email addresses

masks tells apps `email_verified: true` for a confirmed address. So masks trusts an address from a
provider only when one of these is true:

- The address is in the provider's **Email domains**, and the tenant has
  [proven that domain](#sending-a-domain-to-its-provider).
- **Trust the addresses it confirms** is on, and the provider reports the address as confirmed.

Turn on **Trust the addresses it confirms** only for a provider that checks the person holds the
mailbox. SAML has no field for confirmation, so a SAML provider is trusted only for proven domains
in **Email domains it answers for**.

A trusted address lets a provider add an actor with an email address, take up an invitation, or
change an actor's address.

**Email domains** also limit who signs in. When the provider's **Email domains** or the policy's
`email_domains` is set:

- The provider signs in only addresses in both lists. An unset list allows any domain.
- The provider must report the address as confirmed. An address it says nothing about counts as
  confirmed only in a proven domain on the provider's list.
- Someone with no email address is refused.

With neither list set, a provider that adds actors can add someone who has no email address.

### Where a provider is offered

The [sign-in policy](/build/features/#sign-in-policies) decides where a provider is offered:

- `first_factors` must include `provider`.
- `providers` lists which providers. **All providers** offers every one.
- A provider that belongs to an [organization](/build/organizations/#provider) is offered on the
  sign-in page only to a request that names the organization.

A signed-in actor can connect any provider their policy offers under **Connected accounts** on their
account page. They must have signed in within the last 15 minutes. masks refuses an account at the
provider that is already connected to someone else.

### Sending a domain to its provider

An actor who types an email address at a company's domain can go straight to that company's
provider, with no password prompt. masks does this only for a domain the tenant has proven it
controls.

1. In `/manage`, open **Settings**, then **General**.
2. Under **Domains**, enter the domain and choose **Claim**.
3. Publish the TXT record masks shows. A TXT record is a text entry in the domain's DNS settings,
   such as `_masks-challenge.acme.example` with the value `masks-verification=…`.
4. Choose **Check**, or wait for the hourly check.
5. Once the domain is proven, choose **Send to** the provider in the list beside it. **Sign in here**
   turns this off.

After that, an email address at the domain starts the provider's sign-in. This happens even when the
provider belongs to an organization the app did not name. Any other address, and a nickname, sign in
the usual way.

- Claiming a domain needs `masks:manage:security` or `masks:manage`.
- Only one tenant can prove a domain. Another tenant's check for it is refused.
- When the record stops answering, the domain shows **Stopped answering**. Seven days later it is no
  longer proven, and actors sign in the usual way again.
- A sign-in policy without the `provider` factor sends nobody to a provider.

## Provider protocols

### OpenID Connect

masks checks the `id_token` from the provider:

- Its signature, against the issuer's keys.
- Its issuer, against the provider's issuer.
- Its audience and nonce, against the client and the request.

The request uses PKCE, a one-time secret that stops someone else from using the sign-in code.

The subject, the ID for the account at the provider, is `sub` by default. For a Microsoft directory,
**Subject (sub or oid)** on the provider's **Sign-in** tab can name `oid` instead.

Apple sends the actor's name only on their first sign-in. masks keeps it.

### OAuth 2.0

With no `id_token`, masks reads the provider's userinfo endpoint. The request uses PKCE.

- **Where each claim comes from** maps each claim to a path in the response, such as `data.id` for X
  or `id` for GitHub.
- An **Emails URL** lists confirmed email addresses apart from the profile, as GitHub does. masks
  uses the primary confirmed address, or else another confirmed one. It ignores an address that
  appears only in the public profile.

### SAML 2.0

1. In `/manage`, choose **Add provider**, then a SAML known provider or **SAML 2.0**.
2. Give the identity provider the two values under **Give … these**:

   | | |
   | --- | --- |
   | **Assertion consumer service URL** | `https://demo.masks.example/login/provider/<key>/callback` |
   | **Service provider entity ID** | `https://demo.masks.example/login/provider/<key>/metadata`, which also serves masks' metadata |

3. Under **Identity provider**, enter the **Metadata URL** and choose **Read**. Or paste the metadata
   under **Or paste the metadata**.
4. Choose **Add**.

Set **Name ID format** to **Persistent**, or ask the identity provider for a persistent name ID. A
transient name ID changes on every sign-in, so each sign-in looks like a new actor.

masks reads a metadata URL again every night, so it picks up a rotated certificate.

An assertion is the signed message in which the identity provider says who signed in. masks trusts
an assertion only when it:

- is signed by a certificate in the identity provider's metadata
- answers a request this browser sent, and only once
- names this service provider as audience and recipient, and the identity provider as issuer
- is within its validity window, with one minute allowed for clock drift

masks refuses a response it did not ask for, such as one the identity provider starts.

## SAML applications

masks is the identity provider for apps that sign actors in only over SAML 2.0.

1. The app sends an `AuthnRequest`.
2. masks signs the actor in under their [sign-in policy](/build/features/#sign-in-policies).
3. masks posts a signed assertion back to the app.

### What to give the application

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Metadata | `https://demo.masks.example/saml/metadata` |
| Entity ID | The same URL. |
| Single sign-on | `https://demo.masks.example/saml/sso`, HTTP-Redirect or HTTP-POST. |
| Single logout | `https://demo.masks.example/saml/slo`, HTTP-Redirect or HTTP-POST. |
| Certificate | In the metadata. One for each published signing key. |

Most apps need only the metadata URL, which the client's page shows as **masks metadata**. After a
[key rotation](/build/security/#rotating-signing-keys), the app must read the metadata again. The
retiring key's certificate stays in the metadata until that key is retired.

### Registering one

1. In `/manage`, open **Clients**, and choose **Add client**.
2. Choose **Signs actors in over SAML**.
3. Paste the app's metadata under **Its metadata**, and choose **Read it**. masks fills in the app's
   entity ID, assertion consumer services, signing certificate, single logout URL, and whether it
   signs its requests.
4. Choose **Add the client**.

A SAML app is an approved client with no grants and no secret. It cannot use `/authorize` or
`/token`.

The **SAML** section of the client's **General** tab holds its settings:

| Setting | |
| --- | --- |
| **Entity ID** | The `Issuer` its `AuthnRequest` names. |
| **Names actors by** | **A persistent identifier** (pairwise if the client is), or **Their email**. |
| **Its signing certificate** | What masks checks the app's signed requests against. |
| **Attributes it is sent** | One `attribute = claim` a line. Left empty, the app gets the default attributes below. |
| **Refuse requests it did not sign** | Check every request against the certificate. |
| **Let actors start from masks** | Answer `/saml/initiate/<client_id>` without a request. The page shows the path as **Start from masks**. |
| **Single logout URL** | Where masks posts its logout messages. Without one, the app takes no part in [single logout](#single-logout). |

The client's **Endpoints** tab holds its **Assertion consumer services**, the only URLs masks posts
to.

### What is checked

masks shows an error and posts nothing when a request:

- names an `Issuer` with no registered app
- names an assertion consumer service that is not registered, picks one by index, or asks for a
  binding other than HTTP-POST
- asks for a NameID format masks does not issue
- is more than eight minutes old, is more than three minutes in the future, or names another
  `Destination`
- was already received
- fails a required signature check, which needs SHA-256 or stronger
- is larger than 64 kilobytes, or declares a document type

`ForceAuthn` makes the actor sign in again. `IsPassive` gets `NoPassive`, with no page shown. An
actor who is suspended, declines, or is stopped by the policy gets `RequestDenied`.

### What is asserted

The response and the assertion are both signed with RSA-SHA256. The assertion is valid for five
minutes, names the session in `SessionIndex`, and names `https://refeds.org/profile/mfa` when a
second factor was used.

- By default, the attributes are `email`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, and
  `preferred_username`, named after the claims they hold.
- masks releases only what the actor's `openid profile email` consent covers.
- masks releases an email address only once it is confirmed, as an attribute or as the NameID.

masks does not support encrypted assertions, the artifact and SOAP bindings, or choosing an
assertion consumer service by index.

### Single logout

Single logout means that signing out in one place signs the actor out of every app the session used.
An app takes part when it has a **Single logout URL**. masks posts every logout message to that URL
over HTTP-POST, signed with RSA-SHA256.

#### When the app signs a person out

The app sends a signed `LogoutRequest` to `/saml/slo`, over HTTP-Redirect or HTTP-POST. masks
refuses it, and ends nothing, when:

- the app has no single logout URL or no certificate
- the signature is missing or does not verify against the app's certificate
- the request fails the checks an `AuthnRequest` gets, or has expired
- the request names no `NameID`

Otherwise, masks ends every session in which the app was given that NameID. A request that carries a
`SessionIndex` ends only the sessions it names. masks answers with a signed `LogoutResponse`:
`Success`, or `Requester` with `UnknownPrincipal` when nothing matched.

An ended session ends as it does at `/logout`. OpenID Connect clients get their
[back-channel logout](/build/features/#telling-other-apps) tokens, and the session's other SAML
apps are signed out as the next section describes.

#### When a person signs out of masks

Each app with a single logout URL that the session signed in to gets one `LogoutRequest`. It names
the NameID and `SessionIndex` from that app's assertion.

| How the session ends | How the apps hear |
| --- | --- |
| **Sign out**, or an app's `LogoutRequest` from the browser holding the session | The browser visits each app in turn. Then it goes where the logout was going, or back to the app that asked. |
| Any other way, such as a manager signing the actor out, the actor being suspended, or the session timing out | masks posts the `LogoutRequest` to each app from the server. A `2xx` or `3xx` answer counts as delivered. masks tries up to five times, then records a failed delivery as an event. |

A delivery from the server reaches an app without the actor's browser. So it ends only sessions the
app can find by NameID or `SessionIndex`.

## Provisioning

Provisioning means a directory adds, changes, and removes actors in masks for you. A directory such
as Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, or JumpCloud does this over SCIM 2.0
([RFC 7643](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7643),
[RFC 7644](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7644)).

Each tenant's base URL is its issuer followed by `/scim/v2`:

```
https://demo.masks.example/scim/v2
```

### Connecting a directory

1. In `/manage`, open **Settings**, then **Directory**.
2. Under **Provisioning**, enter a label, such as the directory's name.
3. If the tenant has organizations, choose **Every actor**, or **Only members of** one
   [organization](#a-directory-for-one-organization).
4. Choose how long the token lives: **30 days**, **90 days**, or **A year**. The default is 90 days.
5. Choose **Issue a token**, and copy it. masks shows it once.
6. In the directory, enter the **SCIM base URL**, and enter the token as a bearer token. A bearer
   token is a secret that grants access to whoever sends it.

Issuing a token needs `masks:manage:security` or `masks:manage`. Only `masks:manage` can issue one
for every actor, because that token reaches managers too. See
[limits on the narrower roles](/build/security/#limits-on-the-narrower-roles).

Each token shows who issued it, when it was last used, and when it expires. **Revoke** refuses it
from then on.

A client can also provision. The client must:

- be allowed `masks:scim`
- request its own token with [`client_credentials`](/build/features/#signing-in-as-itself)
- name the base URL as its `resource`

### What is provisioned

`/Users` supports reads, filters, creation, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and deletion.

| SCIM | masks |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The actor's `uuid`. |
| `userName` | The nickname, or the email address when it is an email address. |
| `externalId` | Stored and filterable. It is unique in the tenant, or in the organization for a [directory for one organization](#a-directory-for-one-organization). |
| `name`, `displayName` | The name claims. |
| `emails` | The primary email address, treated as confirmed. |
| `phoneNumbers`, `photos`, `profileUrl`, `locale`, `timezone` | The matching claims. |
| `active` | Whether the actor is suspended. |
| `password` | Set, if the directory sends one. |

A provisioned actor holds the standard scopes. They have no password unless the directory sent one.
They sign in through a [provider](#providers) that trusts the same email address, or by accepting
an invitation.

- Filters join up to four comparisons with `and`. `externalId` compares exactly.
- A user's `meta.version` is a weak `ETag`. A `PUT` or `PATCH` whose `If-Match` names an older
  version is refused with `412`.
- `/ServiceProviderConfig`, `/ResourceTypes`, and `/Schemas` describe the rest.
- `/Groups` answers only a [directory for one organization](#roles-as-groups).
- Bulk operations and sorting are not supported.

`active: false` suspends an actor, the same as suspending them in `/manage`. See
[suspending and deleting](/build/features/#suspending-and-deleting). `active: true` restores the
actor. `DELETE` removes them.

A provisioning token changes many accounts. So it cannot:

- set the password or email address of anyone holding a `masks:` scope
- suspend or delete the last active holder of `masks:manage`
- change anyone's scopes

Every change is recorded in the actor's activity, marked as SCIM.

### A directory for one organization

A provisioning token can belong to one [organization](/build/organizations/). Then a customer's
directory manages that customer's actors and nobody else.

| Request | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| List or read users | Only the organization's members. Anyone else is not found. |
| Create a user | A new actor that joins as `member`. Its email address must be at a proven domain that sends actors to one of the organization's providers, and is then treated as confirmed. Any other email address is refused with `400`. A user without an email address is allowed. |
| Replace or patch a user | Allowed only for an actor this directory created who belongs to no other organization and manages nothing. Anyone else is refused with `403`. |
| Delete a user | Removes them from the organization and revokes its tokens. The actor stays. |

Each organization's directory keeps its own `externalId` for each member, so two organizations'
directories can use the same value. An actor's **Access** tab in `/manage` shows them under
**Provisioned**.

A `userName`, email address, or `externalId` that is already taken is refused with `409`. The answer
is the same every time, so it does not say who holds the value or where.

### Roles as groups

A directory for one organization manages roles through `/Groups`. Each of the organization's roles
is one group.

- Its `displayName` is the role.
- Its `id` is the organization's uuid and the role, joined by a dot.
- Its members are the actors who have accepted that role.

| Request | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| List or read groups | Every role, `owner` and `member` included. Filter with `displayName eq` or `id eq`. |
| Add a member | Gives them that role in place of the one they held. |
| Remove a member | Moves them back to `member`. They stay in the organization. |
| Replace members | Adds everyone named and moves everyone else back to `member`. Actors this directory did not create keep their role. |
| Create a group | Adds a role with that name. An existing role is a conflict. |
| Delete a group | Removes the role once nobody holds it. `owner` and `member` cannot be deleted. |
| Rename a group | Refused. |

A group takes only actors this directory created who belong to no other organization and manage
nothing.

- Adding anyone else is refused with `400`, and removing them with `403`. The answer is the same
  whether or not the account exists.
- Removing the last owner is refused with `409`.
- A role change revokes the actor's access tokens for the organization. It is recorded in the
  organization's activity, marked as SCIM.

A token for every actor lists no groups and cannot change them.
